answer: A staking bond works like a marble quarry on a mesa: each identity must lock a costly deposit before it can earn, so spawning thousands of fake agents means paying thousands of bonds. The deposit is a relic of past work, not a free username, and slashing burns it when the agent misbehaves. An attacker can still buy identities, but the price scales linearly with the attack size, while honest agents pay once and keep earning, so faking a majority costs more than the reward it could steal.
